'''Shihoko Ishii''' ({{langx|ja|石井志保子}}, born 1950)<ref>Birth year from [http://www.isni.org/isni/0000000440063831 ISNI authority control file], retrieved 2018-11-28.</ref> is a Japanese mathematician and professor at the [[University of Tokyo]].  Her research area is [[algebraic geometry]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ishii, Shihoko|url=http://www.ams.org/mathscinet/search/author.html?mrauthid=198021|website=MathSciNet|publisher=Mathematical Reviews|accessdate=8 April 2017}}</ref>

==Education==

Ishii received her bachelor's degree from [[Tokyo Women's Christian University]] in 1973 and her master's degree from [[Waseda University]] in 1975.  She later earned her PhD from [[Tokyo Metropolitan University]] in 1983.<ref name="europeansociety">{{cite web|title=Shihoko Ishii|url=http://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/women-in-math/portrait/shihoko-ishii|website=European Women in Mathematics|accessdate=8 April 2017}}</ref>

==Research==

Ishii's research focuses on [[singularity theory]].  She studies arc spaces, a mathematical concept related to [[Jet (mathematics)|jets]]: arc spaces are [[algebraic variety|varieties]] encapsulating information about curves on another variety.<ref name="europeansociety" />

==Awards and honours==

Ishii received the [[Saruhashi Prize]] for accomplishments by a Japanese woman researcher in the natural sciences in 1995.<ref>{{cite book|author1=Sumiko Otsubo|chapter=Women Scientists and Gender Ideology|editor1-last=Robertson|editor1-first=Jennifer|title=A Companion to the Anthropology of Japan|date=2008|page=474}}</ref>  As a postdoc, Ishii was inspired by reading a profile of [[Fumiko Yonezawa]], a physicist and former winner of the Saruhashi prize.<ref name="europeansociety" />

Ishii received the Algebra Prize from the [[Mathematical Society of Japan]] in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|title=Prizes by Research Sections|url=http://mathsoc.jp/en/pamph/current/section_pr.html|website=Mathematical Society of Japan|accessdate=8 April 2017}}</ref>

In 2022, she became a laureate of the [[Asian Scientist 100]] by the ''[[Asian Scientist]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.asianscientist.com/as100/ |title=The Asian Scientist 100 |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= |publisher= [[Asian Scientist]] |access-date= 13 March 2025 |quote= |language= }}</ref>
